open_obligations: Note that time limit, judge pool and number of turns changed together.
Check whether 5 minutes still leaves the passage largely unread.
Compare with pilot timing data used to set the 5-minute limit.
in.other_title: Two-judgment protocol with selected Upwork judges and a 5-minute limit per judgment
in.rationale: Parrish et al. note the 90-second limit is artificial and that 120 seconds might still be too short. The two-turn follow-up keeps the top 16 of 32 pilot judges and sets 5 minutes per judgment, and still reports no significant effect of arguments (2x2x2 ANOVA, no main effects); judge selection and counter-arguments also changed, so time is not isolated.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether a longer judging time changes the debate-argument null result, for human judges on 2-option QuALITY

text: The authors state that the time limit makes the task more artificial than they would like, although pilot results show that varying the limit between 60 and 120 seconds made virtually no difference in performance. They note it is possible that 120 seconds is still too short.
title: Artificial time limit for judges; 60-120 s pilot variations made virtually no difference
